heldClaims.claimText: NTU guidelines state that AI detector tools should be used with caution due to frequent false positives and negatives, ease of bypass, and bias against non-native English writing patterns.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Research shows that the use of AI detector tools should be used with caution due to the following reasons. Unreliable Detection: Frequent false positives (human text flagged as AI) and false negatives (AI text missed). ... Discrimination: Bias against non-native writing patterns (e.g. ESL/EFL students).
evidence.snippetLocation: Use of AI Detector Tools section

topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: NTU’s 2025 statement generally permits assignment AI use, with teacher prohibitions for pedagogical reasons. Current Library guidance requires module instructions and explicit permission for extensive use.
topics.scope: Dated institutional statement and current Library guidance; internal full teaching policy not obtained.

claims.text: NTU’s dated 24 June 2025 statement says GenAI is generally permitted in assignments, but professors may prohibit it for specific pedagogical reasons communicated to students. Students are expected to declare use and how it was used, and remain responsible for accuracy and citations. This is a dated institutional statement, not the complete current internal teaching policy or permission for every assessment.

evidence.quote: NTU’s policy is that in general, students are allowed to use Gen AI in their assignments. Many Schools across STEM and non-STEM disciplines, in medicine, and at NIE, are already using AI as part of learning. Students are expected to declare any use of AI, and how they are being used. When using AI, students are ultimately responsible for the content generated. They must ensure factual accuracy and cite all sources properly. Some professors may prohibit Gen AI for certain assignments for specific pedagogical reasons. In such cases, the reason for disallowing it is clearly communicated to students.
evidence.title: Comment on the use of AI in education | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: Official statement, 24 June 2025; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 9338:9941

claims.text: NTU Library advises students to check instructor and assignment instructions before using AI because expectations vary by module and discipline.

evidence.quote: Expectations around AI use may vary by module and discipline; seek clarification from your instructor or refer to assignment instructions before use.
evidence.title: Guidelines for Responsible Use - Using AI Discovery Tools Responsibly - LibGuides at Nanyang Technological University
evidence.location: Consult; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 572:721

claims.text: NTU Library instructs students to obtain explicit instructor permission for more extensive AI involvement, such as generating source materials or enhancing visuals.

evidence.quote: Obtain explicit permission from your instructor for more extensive AI involvement, such as generating source materials or enhancing visuals.

topics.title: Exams
topics.summary: Do not access AI during exams where external resources are forbidden. Check the exact examination instructions; open-resource exams do not automatically authorise AI.
topics.scope: NTU Library guidance; restriction applies when external resources are not permitted.

claims.text: NTU Library instructs students not to access AI tools during examinations when external resources are not permitted. This condition does not establish either a ban in every exam or automatic AI permission in open-resource exams.

evidence.quote: Follow Exam Protocols. Do not access AI tools during examinations when external resources are not permitted to maintain fair testing conditions.
evidence.title: Guidelines for Responsible Use - Using AI Discovery Tools Responsibly - LibGuides at Nanyang Technological University
evidence.location: Consult, Follow Exam Protocols; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 722:866

topics.title: Disclosure
topics.statusLabel: Disclose use; check the required detail
topics.summary: Disclose AI assistance in submissions and follow module requirements. Detailed prompt/output records and the format depend on the instructor; thesis submissions have a separate Statement of Originality requirement.
topics.scope: Student Library guidance; separate thesis submission declarations.

claims.text: NTU Library instructs students to disclose AI-tool use in their submissions and follow their module’s AI-use policy and instructor guidance. The required level of documentation and disclosure format depend on the assignment and instructor’s expectations; detailed prompt-and-output records and a particular declaration form are not universal requirements.

evidence.quote: Use AI tools to support tasks such as brainstorming, outlining, or checking grammar, but ensure you disclose their use in your submissions. Always refer to your module's AI use policy and seek guidance from your instructor regarding specific expectations for acceptable AI usage in your courses.
evidence.title: Introduction - Using AI Discovery Tools Responsibly - LibGuides at Nanyang Technological University
evidence.location: Key Points on Ethical AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 2828:3123

evidence.quote: When using AI for assignments (e.g., grammar checks, copyediting, or idea generation), adhere to the specific guidelines set by your instructor, as expectations may vary by module and discipline. This may include documenting your AI use, completing a “ Declaration on GAI Use ,” or disclosing AI contributions where required. To uphold academic integrity, you must always provide proper citations for all sources used, including AI‑generated content.
evidence.title: Document, Disclose & Cite AI Usage - Using AI Discovery Tools Responsibly - LibGuides at Nanyang Technological University
evidence.location: Purpose of Documenting, Disclosing and Citing AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 674:1124

claims.text: For some assignments, instructors may require AI process records. NTU Library’s tracking template may be used or adapted when record-keeping is required or recommended, following the instructor’s format and level of detail.

evidence.quote: For some course assignments, instructors may require you to document your AI use. This supports transparency in your learning process and clarifies how AI was used at different stages of your work. Such records may be submitted as an appendix. To support this, NTU Library provides a ready‑to‑use template that outlines what to document. This template may be used or adapted when record‑keeping is required or recommended, while following your instructor’s preferred format and level of detail.
evidence.title: Document, Disclose & Cite AI Usage - Using AI Discovery Tools Responsibly - LibGuides at Nanyang Technological University
evidence.location: Document AI Usage (When Required or Recommended); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 1365:1859

claims.text: From November 2025, NTU’s thesis/dissertation Statement of Originality includes an AI-use disclosure section. The required declarations form part of thesis submission requirements; the source does not establish a single faculty-independent template.

evidence.quote: The following 3 statements are to be included in all theses and dissertations by students: ​ Statement of Originality : Certifies that work done and reported is the student's own and has not been previously submitted to another University or Institution. [New (from Nov 2025)] It includes a section on the disclosure of AI-use in the preparation of the thesis/ dissertation.
evidence.title: Theses / Dissertations | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: Submission Requirements, Statement of Originality, new from Nov 2025; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 3416:3790

topics.title: Privacy & sensitive data
topics.summary: Do not upload protected research data to external GenAI unless legal, restricted-access and no-retention conditions are met, plus owner permission where applicable or RCA agreement. The RCA route does not waive the other safeguards.
topics.scope: Research data; not approval of all institutional tools for sensitive coursework.

claims.text: In research, confidential or sensitive information and personal data must not be uploaded to external GenAI platforms unless all applicable conditions are met: compliance with relevant laws and institutional policies; access restricted to authorised study members; no retention of the data in or by the GenAI; and, where applicable, explicit written permission from the data owner or agreement to that GenAI use in the Research Collaboration Agreement.

evidence.quote: Any confidential or sensitive information, and/or personal data must not be uploaded to any external GenAI software, system, or platform unless: The activity does not contravene any applicable laws, regulations, or institutional policies; Access to the GenAI is controlled and restricted to only authorised study members involved in the research; The data is not retained in or by the GenAI; and Where applicable, written permission has been explicitly provided by the data owner, or the use of such GenAI has been agreed upon in the Research Collaboration Agreement (RCA).
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: §4 Data Privacy & Confidentiality; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 6791:7364

topics.title: Research & publication
topics.statusLabel: Disclose, verify and preserve research integrity
topics.summary: Acknowledge research use beyond basic spelling/grammar checks, retain human authorship and follow stricter recipient rules. Label and document AI visuals; experimental images have explicit methodology exceptions, not permission to fabricate results.
topics.scope: Research proposals, scholarly outputs and theses; original should/must wording remains in evidence.

claims.text: NTU states that generative AI should not be listed as an author of any paper with NTU affiliation, or as a Principal Investigator, Co-PI, or collaborator in research proposals.

evidence.quote: Therefore, GenAI (e.g. ChatGPT) should not be listed as an author of any paper with an affiliation to NTU; or listed as a Principal Investigator (PI), Co-PI, or collaborator in any research proposals.
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: §2 Authorship; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 4365:4565

claims.text: NTU research policy states that GenAI use beyond basic spelling and grammar checks should be acknowledged and cited, identifying the tool’s full name and version, purpose and use in research proposals, manuscripts and scholarly works.

evidence.quote: In the interests of transparency and integrity, the use of GenAI beyond basic spelling and grammar checks should be appropriately acknowledged and cited . This would include acknowledging the use of any AI tools in their research proposals, manuscripts, and scholarly works through a statement specifying the tool's full name and version, its purpose of use, and how it was used.
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: §1 Acknowledging/Declaring the Use of GenAI; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 3334:3713

claims.text: NTU requires AI-generated research images, figures and videos to be clearly labelled and the methods, tools and parameters documented sufficiently for reproducibility.

evidence.quote: All AI-generated images, figures, and videos must be clearly labelled as such. Researchers are required to document the methods, tools, and parameters used to generate these visuals in sufficient detail to ensure reproducibility.
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: §3(i); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 5457:5686

claims.text: AI-generated research visuals must not be presented as actual experimental data unless AI or AI-assisted tools are an essential component of the research design and/or methodology. Using AI to fabricate images resembling experimental results constitutes serious research misconduct.

evidence.quote: AI-generated images, figures and videos must not be presented as actual experimental data unless AI (or AI-assisted) tools are an essential component of the research design and/or methodology. The use of AI to fabricate images to resemble experimental results constitutes serious research misconduct.
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: §3(ii); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 5691:5991

claims.text: NTU prohibits substantive AI modification of genuine experimental images unless clearly described in the methodology.

evidence.quote: Similarly, the substantive modification of genuine experimental images using AI tools is prohibited unless clearly described in the methodology.
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: §3(ii); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 5992:6136

claims.text: When an agency, journal or other receiving party has GenAI rules that differ from NTU research policy, researchers should follow the stricter rules.

evidence.quote: If the proposal, manuscript or other document is being submitted to a agency, journal or other party with rules concerning GenAI that differ from the NTU policy, then the stricter rules should be followed.
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore

additionalTopics.title: Academic integrity
additionalTopics.summary: Misrepresenting AI work is academic misconduct in the Library’s handbook summary. Research plagiarism and research-misconduct referral have their own conditions; referral is not guilt or an automatic sanction.
additionalTopics.scope: Public Library summary and separately scoped research misconduct procedure.

claims.text: NTU Library’s public summary of the 2025 Academic Integrity Handbook states that misrepresenting AI-generated content as one’s own work is academic misconduct. The complete internal handbook was not independently obtained.

evidence.quote: AI tools can assist your thinking but should not replace it; misrepresenting AI-generated content as your own work is considered academic misconduct.
evidence.title: Introduction - Using AI Discovery Tools Responsibly - LibGuides at Nanyang Technological University
evidence.location: Key Points on Ethical AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 2678:2827

claims.text: NTU states that not citing or acknowledging the use of generative AI could be considered plagiarism (a form of research misconduct), especially if GenAI was used to generate ideas or for literature reviews.

evidence.quote: Not citing or acknowledging the use of GenAI could be considered plagiarism (i.e. a form of research misconduct ), especially if GenAI was used to generate ideas or for literature reviews.
evidence.title: NTU Policy on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Research | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: §1 Acknowledging/Declaring the Use of GenAI; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 3714:3902

claims.text: The Vice President (Research) reviews the RIO preliminary report and may take appropriate action, decide whether to invite the Provost to appoint a COI for faculty/research staff, or decide whether to refer a student to the Board of Discipline. This is a research-misconduct process, not an automatic AI penalty or a finding of guilt.

evidence.quote: 4.4.1 The Vice President (Research) shall review the preliminary investigation report from the RIO, who will then take appropriate action (especially in relation to research staff), or decide whether to invite the Provost to appoint a COI to consider the Allegation/ Complaint under the Framework for Investigation and Disciplinary Proceedings for Faculty and Research Staff, or if the Respondent is a student, decide whether to refer to the Board of Discipline, or take any other appropriate action.
evidence.title: Responding to Allegations/ Complaints of Research Misconduct | Research | NTU Singapore
evidence.location: Research misconduct procedures §4.4.1; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 15628:16128
